reviews.review:
This has to be most pretentious story I've  ever encountered in a game. It tries to be both Dark Souls and Destiny at the same time, and this (and the ending especially, oh the ending) is so cringe-inducing… Coldsteel The Hedgehog was more reasonable than this story. Quests are copycats of ones in Dark Souls. You never told what to do and where to go and can fail any of them by just killing random boss. Oh, and there are only three sidequests in the entire game.
Gameplay is ok. I really like TPS, especially mediocre ones, and this one was just right my alley. Hit detection on critical point can be (heh) hit or miss, tracking of  jumping/dashing enemies is absolutely perfect, most of the bosses are easier to kill that regular enemies which in the second half of the game almost all give shields to just make game somewhat challenging; balance is nowhere to be found. Sniper rifles and shotguns are steamrolling everything else. How do you stack 600 damage rifle with 100% critical scaling versus six damage SMG? Well, you don't. Performance is less that stellar. 60 FPS on GTX1080 put a load on it of ~65%, which is way high for game looking this ordinary and drops to 40 in small buildings for some reason.
Overall I can't name anything remarkable about this game, yet I enjoyed it. If you look for third person shooter that's not plagued with story shoved down your throat, endless cutscenes and rolling-between-covers as core gameplay mechanic -- look no longer, this is it! But wait for a good sale.

Immortal Unchained is tough, frustrating at times, but damn I can't stop playing it. Firearms is a souls-like is an interesting combination, one which I hope more game in future try. If you are into souls-like games, this one is definitely worth your time.
